text:
Maria S.: customer reported Go SDK streaming dropped final event after reconnect when auth token rotates quickly. getting partial response, then iterator closes without final fragment. repro + logs below. @Tim L. can you take a look? cc @Eli R.

Tim L.: ping — can you paste client logs and a short repro? is this reproducible in our internal test harness?

Maria S.: minimal logs (client side):
```
I0310 14:35:27.123 sse.go:212] connected (seq=123)
I0310 14:35:28.987 sse.go:345] recv: "data: {\"text\": \"...partial...\"}\n\n"
I0310 14:35:29.002 sse.go:400] auth refresh requested
I0310 14:35:29.014 sse.go:411] reconnecting (token rotated)
I0310 14:35:29.120 sse.go:220] connected (seq=124)
I0310 14:35:29.121 sse.go:360] recv: "data: {\"text\": \"final\"}\n\n"
I0310 14:35:29.122 sse.go:430] client iterator closed: EOF
```

Server side shows final event delivered, but client iterator never yields the "final" chunk (customer sees truncated output). Also they see a stray heartbeat as `:heartbeat\n\n` immediately after reconnect.

Ashish K.: this smells like our Go SDK uses a buffered channel for frames and we close the channel on context cancel without flushing. if reconnect happens fast (token rotation path), the final frame may be queued but never consumed. heartbeat misalignment then causes the iterator to return prematurely.

Tim L.: can you paste a tiny repro? I want to rule out network flakiness.

Maria S.: repro steps (customer):
1) open streaming request with Go SDK
2) after partial output, trigger token rotate (short TTL test env)
3) immediately reconnect path runs
4) final server event arrives within ~100ms of reconnect

Go repro snippet (customer):
```
// simplified: open stream, read next
r := client.Stream(ctx, opts)
for r.Next() {
  fmt.Println(string(r.Data()))
}
// auth rotate triggered externally
```
They can repro locally in ~20/30 runs.

Eli R.: thanks — two things to consider: A) ensure the frame loop flushes buffered items before returning on reconnect/close, B) filter heartbeat lines (`:` prefix) so they don't count as data frames or billing tokens.

Tim L.: quick patch idea:
```
func (s *streamer) shutdown() {
  // on shutdown, drain bufferedFrames and send to iterator chan before close
  for len(s.buf)>0 {
    s.out <- s.buf.pop()
  }
  close(s.out)
}
```
Also make heartbeat handling explicit: if line startsWith(":") continue.

Maria S.: billing question from customer: they saw an extra partial token billed after reconnect. could heartbeat be counted? any short-term mitigation?

Ashish K.: heartbeats should not be billed. if our SDK emits an empty frame or `""` chunk upstream, that might cause a small token charge depending on server tokenization. short-term mitigation: tell them to upgrade to patched client (we can ship a patch), or set a client-side filter to drop `:` lines. also file with billing to check for false positives on tiny empty frames.

SRE-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime patch branch created: `go/sse-drain-fix` — review requested. deploy window 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC.

DeployBot: canary rollout is set to 5% -> 25% -> 100% pending QA signoff.

Tim L.: I'll open a PR with tests that simulate quick token rotate + server final event delivered after reconnect; add a test that ensures iterator yields final frame.

Eli R.: assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml for followups on tokenization/billing edge case. also add an e2e reproducer script under `sdk/go/repros`.

Maria S.: summary for support ticket: repro steps, client logs, server events show final frame sent, probable cause: buffered frames not flushed on reconnect => final fragment dropped; heartbeat misinterpreted as data. proposed resolution: drain buffer on shutdown and ignore `:` heartbeat lines. please escalate billing check for small empty-frame charges.

Tim L.: thanks — I'll post PR link and ETA in this thread.

Maria S.: marking this as P1 for customer-facing truncation. cheers :thumbsup:
